qualification_separated_from_normal_disp.description: dispatch.run_job() fails closed with GovernanceBlocked before any budget reservation if the measured PermissionAdapter identity has no current QUALIFIED native-preauthorization capability, or if a qualification exists but no longer matches the measured identity. Qualifying is now the smallest explicit disposable operation: `mlgo-v2-dispatch qualify-provider --provider ... --profile ... --evidence <raw-stdout.jsonl> --launch-argv <launch-argv.json>`, which parses and validates real captured provider evidence bytes itself (dispatch_governance._validate_qualification_evidence) rather than accepting a caller-supplied hash. Once qualified, normal dispatch uses PermissionAdapter.prepare_native_preauthorization() with no ceremony fallback.
qualification_separated_from_normal_disp.real_evidence: evidence/slice4/qualified-canonical-dispatch/claude-qualification.json and codex-qualification.json - real qualify-provider CLI runs that parsed and validated the round-3 raw-stdout.jsonl/launch-argv.json bytes (zero additional real provider sessions)

real_provider_side_scope_confinement.description: Claude: --allowedTools scopes Write/Edit to the owned worktree glob only, and --disallowedTools Bash is now sent whenever the phase declares no validation commands (previously Bash omission alone was empirically insufficient - round-3 evidence showed a real unrequested Bash tool_use event). Codex: workspace-write sandbox rooted at -C <owned worktree> (OS-level containment, unchanged mechanism, now proven with a negative scenario).
real_provider_side_scope_confinement.real_negative_scenario: evidence/slice4/qualified-canonical-dispatch/ - both real sessions (#11 Claude, #12 Codex) were prompted to also attempt a harmless marker write into a disposable, non-owned foreign project directory. Both attempts were refused by the real native mechanism (Claude: evidence_token claude.cli.permission_denied; Codex: evidence_token codex.cli.sandbox_denied_or_command_failed), the job observed DENIED, and no marker file was ever created in the foreign directory (evidence/slice4/qualified-canonical-dispatch/foreign-project-after.json), while the in-scope notes.py/bug-notes.txt writes inside the owned worktree succeeded normally.

truthful_crash_recovery_state.description: A durable provider-start-attempted.json marker is written immediately before the child process launches, and raw-stdout.jsonl immediately after real provider output is captured. Any exception in _run_job_via_child_transport after governance/reservation now inspects those two markers to deterministically RELEASE (neither marker present - NOT_SENT proven), HOLD (only the start marker present - START_RECONCILIATION_REQUIRED, ambiguous), or SETTLE (raw-stdout.jsonl present - PROVIDER_RESPONSE_OBSERVED, consumption proven). The canonical child path can no longer finish with actual_call_consumed=true while provider_start_state=NOT_STARTED. provider_side_idempotency is now false in the registry (the child transport does not carry/honor a provider-side idempotency key), and persistent_conversation was removed from both child-direct profiles' declared_capabilities (the transport is intentionally one-shot).
truthful_crash_recovery_state.real_evidence: evidence/slice4/qualified-canonical-dispatch/state/runs/qualified-proof-{claude,codex}-r4/v2/jobs/phase-PROOF4-P01-a1-proof/job.json - both real sessions show provider_start_state=PROVIDER_RESPONSE_OBSERVED with actual_call_consumed=true, and both budget reservations SETTLED (not RELEASED/HELD), consistent with a real, non-crashed, fully-observed dispatch
